newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil receives bids for B band concessions.
newsitem.headline: Brazil receives bids for B band concessions.

text.p: Fifteen groups comprising international and Brazilian companies submitted bids to Brazil's Communications Ministry for upcoming concessions to operate B band cellular services, Ministry officials said.
The groups submitted bids for nine of 10 regional concessions on offer, with only one region covering several Northern states failing to attract bidders, they said.

Renato Guerreiro, the Ministry's executive secretary, said he expected the government to take between 30 and 40 days to evaluate the bids on legal grounds, and the financial solidity of the candidates. Then each group's bid and proposed rate structure will be weighed. Government officials hope to sign the first contract by the end of May, he said.

The first two areas to be concessioned, Sao Paulo city and another region incorporating Brazil's center-west region with some Amazonian states, may be operating by December, Guerreiro said. B band services run by private companies should be operating on a Brazil-wide basis by mid-1998.
The opening of the B band services is expected to add between four and five million new cellular subscribers to Brazil's existing two million cellular customers.
Guerreiro said the sale of 10 regional licenses would generate between five and six billion reais to the Treasury, with a further four to five billion reais being invested in new equipment.
The opening up of Brazil's B band services is the first step in the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector.
